solution:
(a) $f'(x) = \frac{-3(4x - 7)}{(2x^2 - 7x + 5)^2}$

$f'(3) = \frac{(-3)(5)}{(18 - 21 + 5)^2} = \frac{-15}{4}$

(b) $f'(x) = \frac{-3(4x - 7)}{(2x^2 - 7x + 5)^2} = 0 \Rightarrow x = \frac{7}{4}$

The only critical point in the interval $1 < x < 2.5$ has $x$-coordinate $\frac{7}{4}$.

$f'$ changes sign from positive to negative at $x = \frac{7}{4}$.

Therefore, $f$ has a relative maximum at $x = \frac{7}{4}$.

(c) $\int_5^{\infty} f(x)\,dx = \lim_{b \to \infty} \int_5^b \frac{3}{2x^2 - 7x + 5}\,dx = \lim_{b \to \infty} \int_5^b \left(\frac{2}{2x - 5} - \frac{1}{x - 1}\right)\,dx$

$= \lim_{b \to \infty} [\ln(2x - 5) - \ln(x - 1)]_5^b = \lim_{b \to \infty} \left[\ln\left(\frac{2x - 5}{x - 1}\right)\right]_5^b$

$= \lim_{b \to \infty} \left[\ln\left(\frac{2b - 5}{b - 1}\right) - \ln\left(\frac{5}{4}\right)\right] = \ln 2 - \ln\left(\frac{5}{4}\right) = \ln\left(\frac{8}{5}\right)$

(d) $f$ is continuous, positive, and decreasing on $[5, \infty)$.

The series converges by the integral test since $\int_5^{\infty} \frac{3}{2x^2 - 7x + 5}\,dx$ converges.

— OR —

$\frac{3}{2n^2 - 7n + 5} > 0$ and $\frac{1}{n^2} > 0$ for $n \ge 5$.

Since $\lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{\frac{3}{2n^2 - 7n + 5}}{\frac{1}{n^2}} = \frac{3}{2}$ and the series $\sum_{n=5}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^2}$ converges,

the series $\sum_{n=5}^{\infty} \frac{3}{2n^2 - 7n + 5}$ converges by the limit comparison test.
